_readme: Target list for resolve.py. 'hint' = a likely ATS slug worth trying first (still verified, never trusted). 'board'/'tenant' = known-good config, skips resolution. 'portal' = not on a standard ATS; use the URL manually. Priority: 1=apply first, 2=strong, 3=wide net.

companies.name: Esusu

ux_research_authorities.label: UX research / usability authorities
ux_research_authorities.note: Research institutes, publishers, and design-education orgs — plus the vendors whose product IS user research. High signal on a UX resume: one line here outweighs most of best_places_to_work. Geography is close to a non-issue — only Forrester (Manhattan), Rosenfeld Media (Brooklyn), and Dscout (NYC office) sit in the NY/NJ area at all, and the rest are remote-first, which location_include already passes. The live constraint is eligibility, not commute: Baymard, IxDF, and Optimal Workshop are based in Denmark and New Zealand, so their 'Remote' postings sail through the filter but may be EU/NZ-only. The first five are also 15-50 person outfits with no standard ATS and no structured summer program; resolve.py will come back empty, and that means 'no job board', not 'no opening'. Reach a named researcher by email with a portfolio.

companies.name: Nielsen Norman Group
companies.note: Jakob Nielsen / Don Norman. ~50 people, fully distributed — no office in NY/NJ, remote by default. Email direct — 'group' is a stopword, so slug guessing generates nielsennorman but never nngroup.

companies.name: Baymard Institute
companies.note: E-commerce UX benchmarking. Copenhagen-based, fully remote, ~60 people across the US and Europe. Remote roles may be EU-scoped — confirm US eligibility before investing time.

companies.name: Rosenfeld Media
companies.note: Brooklyn (457 3rd St). Publisher + Advancing Research and DesignOps Summit conferences. ~10 people, so 'Brooklyn office' means the founder is in Brooklyn. Conference volunteering is the realistic way in.

companies.name: Interaction Design Foundation
companies.note: Design education. Aarhus, Denmark; fully remote, team on every continent. Remote roles may be EU-scoped — confirm US eligibility.

companies.name: Center for Civic Design
companies.note: Election and civic usability. Fully distributed across the US since founding, ~16 people. Overlaps civic_tech — don't double-apply.

companies.name: Forrester
companies.note: NYC office at 1180 Avenue of the Americas (HQ Cambridge MA). Analyst firm with a real CX/UX research practice, and the one org in this category running a formal internship program. Best probe-budget spend here.

companies.name: UserTesting
companies.note: Research platform. HQ Bellevue WA, remote-first; the NYC presence is coworking-scale, not a hiring hub.

companies.name: Dscout

companies.name: Optimal Workshop
companies.note: Card sorting / tree testing. Wellington, New Zealand. Remote roles may be NZ/AU-scoped — confirm US eligibility.

companies.name: Maze
companies.note: Rapid usability testing. Fully remote with no central office anywhere.

government_portals._note: These are NOT on standard ATS platforms. Each needs its own handling; several are already wired into internship_watch.py or listed here for manual checking.

automated.name: USAJOBS (federal, incl. Pathways Internship Program)
automated.how: built into internship_watch.py — needs a free API key from developer.usajobs.gov

automated.name: NYC Jobs (all city agencies)
automated.how: NYC Open Data publishes current job postings as a dataset with a Socrata API — see resolve.py --gov

manual.note: City digital services + design. Best NYC civic UX entry point.

manual.name: MTA
manual.note: Has a formal internship program; large customer-experience org.

manual.name: United Nations
manual.note: NYC HQ. UN internships are typically unpaid — check before investing time.

government_portals.note_on_federal_digital: 18F and the U.S. Digital Service were the classic federal design-research entry points. Both were significantly restructured during 2025 — verify current status before building them into your pipeline. The private civic-tech contractors in the civic_tech category do much of the same work and hire more predictably.
